subject: AlderBank hosted latency SLO proposal & temporary measurement accommodations
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@alderbank.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@alderbank.com>, procurement@alderbank.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API latency commitments — target p50/p95 & measurement window

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — AlderBank’s product team liked the throughput characteristics. Before we move to a procurement LOI, legal and procurement have asked for explicit latency commitments for the hosted API. High-level asks:

- p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 450ms for text-generation (typical tokens per request ~60)
- Measurement window: rolling 24h with monthly aggregation 
- Evidence package for the first 90 days of production (logs, sampling dashboards)

We understand there can be transient bursts. AlderBank’s security team will want a short-term accommodation if you have scheduled infra events or a migration during our onboarding. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:

1) Accept the p50/p95 targets above for the standard hosted plan?
2) Provide a documented measurement window and sampling methodology that legal can attach to the contract?
3) Offer a temporary carveout policy during onboarding/migration with defined milestone-based remediation?

We’d also like a short outline of the rollback/fallback behavior (model variant routing/fallback to lower-capacity instances) in case of regional degradation.

Thanks,

Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Partnerships
AlderBank

---

Sanjay — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. Short answers up front: yes to 1 and 2, and we can support a narrow, milestone-driven carveout for 90 days as requested.

High-level proposal:
- Commitment: p50 <= 100–120ms, p95 <= 400–500ms (region-dependent). We'll publish the regional baseline in the SOW.
- Measurement: rolling 1h windows aggregated to daily and monthly reports (we log raw per-request latencies; contract attaches our sampling/playbook).
- Temporary carveout: a 90-day onboarding carveout that allows a windowed tolerance (p95 up to 650ms) for at most 5 business days total during that period, provided milestones are met (onboarding health checks and traffic ramp milestones).

We’ll provide an evidence package (see attached sample) and a canned dashboard link for your audits. Ben and Karthik are looped in for pricing and technical measurement language.

Next steps: I can share a draft contract paragraph and the measurement appendix by tomorrow. Are you available for a 30-min call on Friday to lock the carveout milestones?

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Sanjay, Lauren — quick technical clarifications from our side to ensure the measurement language is deterministic: 

1) Metric definition: latency measured server-side end-to-end (receipt -> first byte emitted). We exclude client-side network time.
2) Request classes: we'll classify by token-count buckets (<=64, 65–256, >256). Contract targets will apply to the <=64 bucket by default; other buckets get documented baselines.
3) Rolling window: we compute p50/p95 on rolling 1h shards and then take a weighted daily aggregation for month-level reporting. This handles bursty traffic while allowing short-lived spikes to be visible in hourly telemetry.

Carveout mechanics we propose: each carveout event must be logged and supported with an incident postmortem and two remediation checkpoints (ops runbook review, capacity increase). If more than two carveouts are needed, we propose an SLA remediation plan rather than automatic crediting.

We can also enable KV-cache warmup and prioritized batching during AlderBank’s onboarding window to reduce cold-start p95 risk.

— Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Sanjay/Priya — thanks for reviewing. Per our internal alignment with Ben and Karthik, here is the contract-ready paragraph we can include in the SOW and the onboarding appendix (short form):

"Redwood will commit to a regional hosted API baseline of p50 <= 120ms and p95 <= 450ms for standard text-generation requests (<=64 tokens) measured server-side. Latency percentiles are computed on rolling 1-hour windows and aggregated to daily and monthly reporting. During the first 90 calendar days of production, Redwood may invoke a documented onboarding carveout allowing up to 5 business days where the p95 target may be up to 650ms, subject to milestone verification and incident postmortems. All carveout events will be recorded in the shared audit Drive and accompanied by a remediation plan."

If that language looks good, Ben will provide the pricing addendum tied to the carveout and I can get the legal language to your counsel. If you want a narrower measurement window (e.g., rolling 15m windows), we can discuss tradeoffs — shorter windows show spikes but increase false positives for transient infra noise.

Would you like me to send the SOW paragraph to your counsel directly or route via your procurement contact?

— Lauren
